EICMA 2026 • Honda CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports Is a Tongue Twister, Weighs Less but Offers More
I Drove It to My Garage in 1999 and Abandoned It: 1972 Pontiac Is a Forgotten Restoration Candidate
29 photos
Photo: eBay seller dmcal5
I drove the car to my garage in 1999, and it’s been sitting ever since. This is the description the seller of this 1972 Pontiac Firebird posted on eBay, trying to convince Internet strangers to take it home.
While this Pontiac has been sitting for so many years, it still looks doable. Sure, it’s not an easy project, and more importantly, it requires extensive work in all key areas, but with the right fixes, it would eventually become a head-turner.
The owner posted the car for auction, but a reserve has also been completed. Few specifics were shared, and I have no idea how much you need to bid to unlock the reserve. But what I do know is that the battle could soon become fiercer than expected.
Photo: eBay seller dmcal5 The 1972 Pontiac Firebird production nearly collapsed from the previous year, and it’s not because the car was no longer appealing to American buyers. Unfortunately for the Firebird, it ended up becoming a collateral victim of the UAW strike at the Norwood, Ohio plant where the Firebird and the Camaro were produced.
The strike ended after 174 days, and despite Pontiac resuming Firebird production afterwards, it ended the year with only 29,951 units rolling off the assembly line.
The base Firebird continued to be the top version in the lineup with 12,001 units, while the Esprit was the runner-up with 11,415 cars. The Formula was third in the charts with 5,249 cars, while the Trans Am was less popular than in the previous year and accounted for only 1,286 units. The Trans Am didn’t yet take off, and the strike certainly impacted its output.
The Trans Am continued to be offered with a 455 HO, once again with a manual and an automatic. The manual was the more popular choice, accounting for 458 orders.
Photo: eBay seller dmcal5 Otherwise, the Firebird could be had with a 250ci six-cylinder engine, while a 350 two-barrel was optional. This optional engine was standard on the Esprit, this time with a 400 two-barrel being listed as optional. The Formula 400 continued this year with a 400 four-barrel, while the Formula 455 was fitted from the factory with the same 455 installed on the Trans Am.
This Firebird left the factory with the Esprit package, being fitted with a 400ci V8 engine and a two-barrel carburetor. It was paired with a 400 automatic transmission.
The engine is no longer running, though it was in much better shape in 1999 when the owner drove it to their garage and parked it for eternity. The car has “not started or moved since then,” the seller explains in the post on eBay.
My recommendation is that you ask for more details about the engine under the hood because it’d be a shame to give up on the factory 400 that is still under the hood. The seller says the car is complete and original, so you should certainly give the factory 400 a second chance.
If you don’t live very far from the owner’s location, you should just send your mechanic to inspect it in person, as this is the only way to figure out all details and determine your chances of saving the engine. My guess is that an engine rebuild would do it, but you know this for sure unless you see the engine with your own eyes.
Photo: eBay seller dmcal5 The body looks good, but it wears previous accident damage. Some body parts were replaced with 1974 panels and lights, but the correct 1972 components are also included.
These aren’t the only extras that you’ll be getting if you buy this car. The Firebird also comes with two keys, the original Pontiac service manual, the owner’s manual, a title, the build sheet, and the sales brochure. This is fantastic news for someone who wants to restore the car to the day-one configuration, as all of these make this Firebird a small piece of automotive history.
There are also maintenance receipts, with the seller explaining that they appear to be complete, although they haven’t investigated this further.
It’s time to discuss the thing that could end up becoming a roadblock for this Firebird’s return to the road. The owner wants to sell the car at auction, with the bidding starting at $200, though considering a reserve is also in place, the selling price is likely much higher. No further specifics were shared, but considering the auction ends in 9 days, it’ll be interesting to see how high the bidding goes.
The vehicle is parked in Saint Louis, Missouri, and considering it no longer runs, you will need transportation to move it from its current parking location to your garage. As a result, make sure you also consider shipping costs, especially because you’ll get some extras, and a large trailer is the only option for the winning bidder.

source_document.body:
EICMA 2026 • Triumph TF-E Bikes Get Even More Enduro With Updates for the 2027 Model Year
2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive Spends Fewer Than 3 Hours Charging on Its Way From Norway to Spain
8 photos
Photo: BMW
Driving a zero-emission car from the top of Norway to southern Spain involves more than sufficient battery capacity to cover the distance. From the route between charging stations to traffic and weather conditions, a lot of things can make a substantial difference between the time spent driving and charging.
BMW wanted to demonstrate how its latest electric vehicle technologies can handle those variables by sending a production-spec i3 50 xDrive on the Paneuropeana route, which involves covering 5,886.7 kilometers (3,658 miles) across eight countries. On its route, the i3 50 xDrive in question required merely 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds of DC fast charging.
The journey started at North Cape on the Norwegian island of Mageroya, where a headland extends into the Arctic Ocean. At the other end of the route, the full-electric Bimmer reached Tarifa in Spain's Andalusian province of Cadiz. In other words, the southernmost point of mainland Europe. A considerable geographical spread, for sure, with said route connecting two very different places.
North Cape and Tarifa couldn't be much farther apart within continental Europe, and this journey is all the more relevant because it subjected the i3 50 xDrive to a variety of road and weather conditions along the way. BMW claims the subject vehicle covered ordinary country roads, motorways, and urban stretches, with the organizers choosing checkpoints that prioritize normal road use instead of speed.
All in all, the team had to balance three distinct variables: driving distance, energy consumption, and charging performance. The objective here wasn't to achieve the shortest possible journey time at any cost, but to minimize the accumulated time connected to chargers.
Photo: BMW The i3 in question spent a whopping 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes actually driving, whereas the chargers used along the way filled up the high-voltage battery of the 50 xDrive at an average of 275 kilowatts. Better still, the Bavarian automaker quotes 12.5 kilowatt-hours for every 100 kilometers (62 miles) as the average energy consumption on this route, which is below the WLTP-rated consumption range of 13.4 to 18.0 kWh/100 km.
Average speed? Make that 79.7 kilometers per hour, which is 49.5 miles per hour in the United Kingdom and the United States of America. The Munich-based manufacturer also claims this result beats the Paneuropeana charging time record from 2017 by more than seven hours, with the previous record holder being a Tesla Model S 100D that clocked 9 hours and 51 minutes.
Under the skin, the i3 50 xDrive packs two electric drive units with combined maximum output ratings of 463 horsepower and 476 pound-feet (645 Newton-meters) of twist, enabling the compact luxury sedan to hit 100 kilometers per hour (62 miles per hour) in 4.7 seconds. Capable of hitting 200 kph (124 mph), the i3 50 xDrive is rocking 108.7 kilowatt-hours of usable capacity.
Benefiting from a cell-to-pack architecture, said high-voltage battery uses cylindrical cells instead of the previous-gen prismatic design. The 800-volt electrical system and this gen-six battery enable a maximum DC charging power of 400 kilowatts, with BMW claiming that 10 minutes of charging on direct current will get you 423 kilometers (263 miles) of WLTP range.

EICMA 2026 • Honda Africa Twin Gets Biggest Refresh in a Decade, They Now Call It CRF1150L
This 1955 Greyhound Scenicruiser Bus Is Now a Spacious Motorhome With Scenic Views
14 photos
Photo: Famous Whip Sales/Instagram
In the whole of American automotive history, few buses have looked as futuristic as the Greyhound Scenicruiser. Developed through a collaboration between the Greyhound Bus Company and General Motors, this two-level bus was introduced in 1954 and became a symbol of cross-country travel in the era.
Able to carry as many as 45 passengers, it stood out with its monocoque construction, aircraft-inspired aluminum body, a raised rear passenger deck, and panoramic windows that gave passengers upstairs great vistas of the passing scenery. It looked nothing like an ordinary highway bus, and it also offered a new level of comfort to long-distance travel, with amenities such as air conditioning, reclining seats, and even an onboard bathroom.
With a short production run of just two years, only 1,001 examples of this iconic bus were ever produced by General Motors, including the rebuilt 1953 prototype. They represented the backbone of Greyhound’s fleet until the mid-1970s, after which they were gradually retired from active service. After years of carrying passengers across the country, second-hand units were used by schools, churches, and charter operators.
Only about 213 examples of the Scenicruiser have survived to this day, and just around 40 are believed to remain roadworthy. Many of those were restored by enthusiasts into motorhomes. This is also the case of the GMC Greyhound Scenicruiser PD-4501 featured here, which got a second lease on life as a recreational vehicle and is currently looking for a new owner.
Photo: Famous Whip Sales/Instagram Built in 1955, this example is serial number 553, and though it doesn’t have its original interior with ten passenger seats on the lower level and another 33 seats on the raised rear deck anymore, it is still a remarkable piece of American highway travel history . At 40 feet (12.2 meters) long and 11 feet (3.3 meters) high, it offers a generous interior volume, making it a great platform for custom luxurious motorhome conversions. The raised rear deck with panoramic windows, modeled after 1950s train dome cars, also add to its appeal.
On the outside, the split-level, "deck-and-a-half" design, tandem rear axles, and signature fluted stainless-steel lower body make it instantly recognizable. However, the custom paint job applied after the bus was converted into a motorhome and several other details, such as two rooftop air-conditioning units, make it different from how it left the factory.
Original Scenicruiser buses featured the classic Greyhound white-and-blue color scheme featuring the running dog logo and “Scenicruiser” script along the sides. Instead of the original factory livery, this unit showcases a custom navy blue, cream, and light blue palette with painted arrows and a scenic mural on the upper body. To create a more private interior, several lower-level and upper-deck windows were paneled over and painted to match the rest of the exterior.
Photo: Famous Whip Sales/Instagram The Scenicruiser’s interior has been transformed into a true home on wheels with separate living, dining, kitchen, and sleeping areas. Each area looks comfortable and functional, but the lounge area is particularly interesting. It’s disposed on two levels, with a beige sofa and two matching armchairs located on the lower level at driver height, and a second sofa on the upper level, taking advantage of the bus’s elevated rear section and its panoramic windows.
Opposite the second sofa, there is a dining setup with booth-style seating and a central wooden table with integrated cup holders, while a television provides entertainment.
Photo: Famous Whip Sales/Instagram A narrow hallway with wooden closets on both sides leads toward the kitchen, which boasts an U-shaped layout and is well-equipped for cooking on the road. Wooden cabinetry provide ample storage and the white countertops integrate a stainless-steel double sink. A blue tile backsplash give it a modern look, and appliances like a built-in cooktop, an overhead microwave, and a large stainless-steel refrigerator, ensure full functionality.
The bathroom is equally practical, with blue tiled walls, a toilet, a wood-framed medicine cabinet, and a vanity that integrates a dark marble-look countertop with an oval sink. As in most bus conversions, the main sleeping quarters are at the rear, offering some separation from the main living area.
At the front, the driver area is largely unchanged, except from a new driver’s seat, while a cream two-seat bench with seatbelts is fitted nearby, ensuring safe transportation for two more passengers.
Photo: Famous Whip Sales/Instagram When it comes to the underpinnings that keep this Scenicruiser bus running, the current owner says the original powertrain was replaced in 2010 with a Detroit Diesel 8V92 two-stroke V8, nicknamed the "Screaming Demon." The engine is paired with a heavy-duty Allison automatic transmission.
According to the listing, the bus rides on brand-new heavy-duty tires and tens of thousands of dollars were invested in preventive maintenance since 2019. It also mentions the bus has a multi-generational, single-family history, having originally been purchased directly from Greyhound.
It’s not known when this 1955 Greyhound Scenicruiser bus was transformed into a home on wheels, but now it’s offered for sale out of West Bend, Wisconsin, by Famous Whip Sales. The asking price is $74,900. Vezi această postare pe Instagram O postare distribuită de (Listing Agency) You drive it we list it! (@famouswhips_usa)

source_document.body:
EICMA 2026 • Honda Africa Twin Gets Biggest Refresh in a Decade, They Now Call It CRF1150L
Car Nut Restores Classic Hemi Mopar, Wife Finds the Bill, He Takes Her to Hawaii To Forgive Him
40 photos
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat
Remember, remember, the 30th of November, the Mopar disgrace and collapse; I can show you one reason for the De Soto treason to never be forgot. This paraphrase for the famous rhyme about the 5th of November 1605 plot and attempt to blow up the English parliament would probably describe in a very poetic nuance what happened to De Soto, Chrysler’s undecided division that was abruptly terminated on November 30, 1960. If this 1966 Sportsman Fireflite could talk…
Walter P. Chrysler founded the DeSoto division on August 4, 1928, introducing the brand for the 1929 model year to fill the mid-priced market gap between Dodge and Chrysler. The marque took its name from 16th-century Spanish conquistador Hernando de Soto, who led the first European expedition deep into modern United States territory and crossed the Mississippi River. DeSoto built over 2,000,000 vehicles before abruptly ceasing production in November 1960 and cancelling the division.
Throughout the 1950s, DeSoto reshaped its catalog during Detroit's horsepower wars. The division opened the decade with the 6-cylinder DeLuxe and Custom series, joined in 1952 by the V8-powered Firedome. In 1953, the 6-cylinder Powermaster replaced the DeLuxe and Custom until V8 power became standard in 1955. The flagship Fireflite debuted in 1955, followed by the high-output Adventurer in 1956, the Dodge-based Firesweep in 1957, and the export Diplomat.
Styled under Virgil Exner's Forward Look philosophy, the Fireflite debuted in 1955 as DeSoto's premier luxury series, sitting above the Firedome and yielding only halo status to the limited-production Adventurer. Across its six-year run through 1960, the Fireflite offered four-door sedans, two-door convertibles, six-passenger Shopper and nine-passenger Explorer station wagons, and pillarless two-door and four-door hardtops carrying the “Sportsman” moniker from 1955 through 1959.
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat For the 1955 model year, total DeSoto output surged 50 percent compared to previous year, to 115,485 cars, all riding on a 126-inch (3.2-meter) wheelbase and measuring 218 inches (5,535 millimeters) long. Buyers chose between a standard column-shifted 3-speed manual , a $108 overdrive unit, or a 2-speed PowerFlite automatic ($189).
The entry-level Firedome accounted for 77,760 units, comprising 46,388 four-door sedans, 28,944 Special and Sportsman two-door hardtops, 1,803 wagons, and 625 convertibles. Every 1955 DeSoto carried a 291-cubic-inch (4.8-liter) Hemi V8 with a 7.5:1 compression. While the two-barrel Firedome produced 185 horsepower (188 PS) and 245 lb-ft (332 Nm), the four-barrel Fireflite delivered 200 horsepower (203 PS) at 4,400 rpm and 274 lb-ft (371 Nm), at 2,800 rpm.
The upscale lineup consisted of 26,637 4-door sedans, 10,313 Sportsman hardtops, and 775 convertibles. From 1955 to 1959, DeSoto built 45,959 badged Fireflite Sportsman hardtops, comprising 30,276 two-doors and 15,683 four-door models. After 10,313 two-door units in 1955—the best year for the two-door hardtop—output reached 10,829 in 1956, with 7,479 two-doors and 3,350 four-doors.
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat Combined production peaked in 1957 at 13,943 cars, split between 7,217 two-doors and 6,726 two-doors, fell to 6,527 in 1958, and hit a worst-year low of 4,347 in 1959.
DeSoto dropped the Sportsman badge in 1960 while adding 3,494 two-door and 1,958 four-door Fireflite hardtops. Weighing 3,890 pounds (nearly 1.8 tons), the 1955 Fireflite Sportsman accelerated from 0 to 60 mph / 97 kph in 11 seconds, ran the quarter-mile in 18 seconds, and topped 110 mph, or 177 kph. Priced at $2,939 new, it challenged the Buick Century Riviera, Oldsmobile 98 Holiday, Mercury Montclair, and Packard Constellation.
A surviving 1955 DeSoto Fireflite Sportsman recently starred on the Classic Car ChitChat YouTube channel, where host Kevin Chauhan interviewed the longtime owner in Ontario, Canada. Bruno, a retired licensed mechanic, bought the Los Angeles-built California coupe, roughly 15 years ago. His passion began in childhood while riding in a similar 1955 Chrysler owned by his uncle, a police officer in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat Bruno disassembled the rust-free California hardtop at home before sending it on its solid frame for a single repaint in its factory two-tone green and white scheme. Re-plating the toothy grille, bumpers, and trim proved so costly that when his wife found the chrome bill, Bruno had to take her to Hawaii. The exterior retains its Southern California auto club decal, pivoting door handles, manual cowl vent, and original wire wheels.
Under the hood sits the original 291 Hemi V8 with its glass fuel sediment bowl. Bruno optimistically estimates output at 220 to 225 horsepower, noting that period dual-quad and mechanical-lifter upgrades reached 270 horsepower (274 PS), and idled so roughly the service manual warned mechanics not to bother smoothing it out. After an exhaust manifold failed, he added powder-coated headers and dual exhaust pipes.
Because a 6-volt wiring harness cost $2,000 versus $400 for a 12-volt kit, Bruno converted the electrical system to 12 volts, installing an alternator while leaving the gutted generator housing in place. The higher voltage burned out the 6-volt wiper motor, prompting him to remove the mono radio for access and seek a 1956-model 12-volt motor. For safety, he also upgraded the original single-pot power brakes to a dual-reservoir master cylinder.
Photo: YouTube/Classic Car ChitChat Inside the tri-material green and white cabin, the 2-speed PowerFlite automatic uses a dashboard-mounted Flite-Control selector lever that lacks a Park position. When Bruno stepped out after revving the V8 for Kevin, the 95k-mile coupe began rolling backward until Bruno lunged inside to pull the under-dash handbrake handle, which clamps a drum behind the transmission.
After 15 years of stewardship, Bruno is ready to pass on his work in progress and has placed the 1955 DeSoto Fireflite Sportsman up for sale through Kevin at Classic Car ChitChat. While Bruno has not listed a public asking price, inviting mechanically inclined buyers with indoor storage to message the channel with offers, comparable driver-quality 1955 Fireflite Sportsman hardtops currently command between $20,000 and $35,000 on the collector market.

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
UK-Spec Ford Ranger Raptor V6 EcoBoost Hits 621 BHP With Stage 3 Kit That Includes Garrett Turbos
12 photos
Photo: Motorsport and Performance
As you're well aware, the Ranger Raptor with the 3.0-liter EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 can't do better than 288 brake horsepower from the factory due to gasoline particulate filters indirectly mandated by strict emission standards. UK-based tuner Motorsport and Performance, however, can fix that. Opting for the Stage 3 kit can unleash up to 621 brake horsepower, which is quite a tremendous jump.
Advertised with anything from 600 to 630 ponies, the Stage 3 package builds on two lesser stages. The first one involves only software, with customers offered a choice between 400, 450, and 475-bhp calibrations. The 450 appears to be the most popular, or so claims Motorsport and Performance big kahuna Ben Dunn.
Stage 2 involves new hardware, including an upgraded intercooler that better controls intake air temperature under sustained boost. A cold air intake and MAP x Keltec catted downpipes also need mentioning, along with estimates of 520 to 540 brake horsepower. Upgrading to Stage 3 status requires new turbochargers.
A pair of Garrett-supplied snails are on the menu, specifically PowerMax GT1752S units. The direct-fit spinny lads are said to flow 18 percent more air compared to factory turbos, and the Stage 3 upgrade further replaces the factory-issue plastic charge pipes with aluminum hot- and cold-side piping. Under increased boost pressure, going for aluminum sounds like a very good idea.
Building on the Stage 2 kit, Stage 3 also comes with bespoke engine and transmission control unit calibrations. The customer who supplied the development Ranger Raptor also specified a Manta turbo-back exhaust system, which definitely sounds better than the stock exhaust. High-flow cats are featured, allowing the six-cylinder lump to exhale better.
Photo: Motorsport and Performance This Manta exhaust retains the bi-modal exhaust valves from the factory, so the driver can switch between quiet and rowdy whenever they feel like it. Motorsport and Performance lists the Stage 3 package at 10,499 pounds sterling, whereas the aftermarket exhaust adds another 2,400 on top.
Customers are required to allow one to two weeks for installation and calibration. Fuel choice also matters here, with the British tuner specifying 99-RON E5 gasoline while warning against E10, 95-RON, and 97-RON fuels. Motorsport and Performance further acknowledges that replacing the factory turbos will affect the manufacturer's warranty.
Priced from £51,650 (excluding value-added tax) in the United Kingdom, the Ranger Raptor is advertised by its maker with a 0-60 time of 7.9 seconds. Previously offered with a twin-turbo diesel inline-four mill, the Ranger Raptor lost its lesser diesel engine in early 2026.
Speaking of which, the 2.0-liter EcoBlue was discontinued from all trims in favor of two alternatives. The 3.0-liter EcoBlue remains on sale in the Old Continent, yet Ford of Europe wants prospective customers to believe that the 2.3-liter EcoBoost plug-in hybrid is the direct replacement for the 2.0-liter EcoBlue.
The 3.0-liter EcoBlue is the better choice for maximum towing and payload capacities, offering better highway range than the plug-in hybrid once its high-voltage battery depletes. The six-pot diesel also makes a lot more sense because it produces maximum torque from 1,750 revolutions per minute, giving it effortless and predictable pulling power.

This week on The Loadstar Podcast , we unpack the latest developments in US tariffs and customs enforcement, including tougher rules for foreign importers of record and what a Democrat-controlled Congress could mean for President Trump’s trade agenda.
CargoTrans co-CEO Nunzio De Filippis joins us to explain the implications for importers, while The Loadstar ‘s Alex Lennane discusses the ‘dire’ situation facing European hauliers, why supply chain disruption is forcing shippers into costly emergency airfreight, and the impact of cargo bottlenecks at Bangkok and Shenzhen airports.

This Widebody Lamborghini Temerario Looks Like a Gentleman’s Supercar
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | 1016industries
Did you somehow think that we have covered the Lamborghini Temerario so extensively that there is nothing more to be said about it? Well, that may be partially true, but that does not mean that we cannot put the spotlight on the occasional example that deserves to celebrate its 15 minutes of online fame.
Speaking of that, the one pictured above definitely fits the bill, as it certainly looks a lot more exciting than the stock one. One of the first things that makes it stand out compared to the standard Temerarios is the satin green look. The color is said to be the OEM Verde Hydra Matte, and was applied to all body panels, making this machine look like a veritable gentleman’s supercar, as mentioned in the title.
If you look at the pictures shared in the gallery, then you will see that there are also some black details here and there. However, these do not provide that much contrast, but the bronze wheels do. These feature a turbine-like design, spin around the orange brake calipers, and have been shod in sticky rubber from Michelin. The alloys are said to be a new addition to the 1016 Industries portfolio, and they are definitely not the only thing to have come from the quoted tuner when it comes to the Lamborghini Temerario in question.
That’s because the supercar also benefits from their 1016 Vision Widebody Kit, which makes it look a lot more aggressive. Things such as the front fender attachments, the add-ons on the sides of the OEM front bumper, and the chin spoiler are new, and as you can clearly see, so is the front hood with its vented design close to the windscreen. The side skirts are also new, and they feature some blades at the rear, thus mirroring the look of the splitter.
Photo: Instagram | 1016industries Further back, this Lamborghini Temerario features new trim surrounding the rear air intakes on the outer edges. The wing that rests on the rear deck is also new, and so is the diffuser, complete with its extra brake light mounted in the middle. The add-ons that are part of the tuner’s widebody kit have been made of carbon fiber, and they sport a naked look here, thus making the supercar appear even more aggressive.
Care to talk about the interior? Well, so do we, but unfortunately, it hasn’t opened up to the camera in the images that @1016industries shared on Instagram earlier this week. Thus, it is likely that the cabin hasn’t been modified, and from what we can see by zooming in through the windows in certain pictures, it appears to be mostly black, though there should be some contrasting elements on deck. That’s what we think, anyway.
The enhanced look of this particular Lamborghini Temerario is not joined by a power boost, or if it is, then 1016 Industries hasn’t said anything about it. But that does not make the supercar any less exciting, because it already dwarfs its predecessors, regardless of the configuration, in terms of power and performance, and for what it’s worth, it gets very close to the larger, punchier, and a lot more expensive Revuelto.
That’s because it has 907 hp (677 kW/920 ps) to play with in total. The Temerario features a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 engine, assisted by three electric motors. The 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) is a 2.7-second affair, and it will do 213 mph (343 kph) where the road and legislation allow it.
Photo: Instagram | 1016industries If you want to spruce up your weekend drives, or maybe your daily ones if you do not need something more practical for that, with a brand new Lamborghini Temerario , then you will have to pay from close to $400,000 for such a thing. Highly-optioned examples tend to exceed $450,000 and sometimes half a million dollars, so you must have really deep pockets if this model sits at the very top of your shopping list.
The Temerario debuted more than two years ago, and it entered production in 2025. So far, Lamborghini offers a single version of its new-age “baby” supercar, the two-door coupe, but that’s about to change, as the Raging Bull is getting ready to unveil the second body style.
We are talking about the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder , which was recently teased ahead of its official unveiling scheduled for November 18, in Los Angeles. That is when the company will release the full details, including the acceleration time, top speed, and others, while also delving into the characteristics of its power-folding roof that stows away in a special compartment behind the seats.
The open-top model will feature the same powertrain as its fixed-roof sibling, in the same configuration, but due to the added weight, it should be a tiny bit slower.
Now, that does not really matter in this story, as what does is whether you like the tuned Temerario pictured above. So, do you? Because I definitely do! View this post on Instagram A post shared by 1016 Industries (@1016industries)

Volkswagen Apparently Makes Just €12 Per Vehicle While Mercedes Earns €4,198
27 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
A carmaker that sells nearly six million vehicles in the span of nine months should have more to show for it than 12 euros in operating earnings per car. That's where the Volkswagen Group ended up in the latest financial comparison from the Center of Automotive Management, which covers January 2026 through September 2026. The industry average, by comparison, stood at 1,363 euros.
Mercedes-Benz earned 4,198 euros per vehicle during this period, while BMW reached 3,059 euros. Why does the Wolfsburg-based manufacturer's result look this ugly? Part of the reason comes in the form of an €8.7 billion accounting burden. Without these special charges, the group's margin would have been 3.8 percent.
The CAM report examines 21 automotive manufacturers in total, with CAM using operating EBIT rather than net profit. In other words, the figures presented by the Center of Automotive Management should not be confused with the money automakers retain after every single expense, tax, and financing cost. Even with this distinction, Volkswagen's position is well-nigh impossible to defend.
Its 12-euro figure puts the group near the bottom of the list, below Stellantis at 250 euros and three Chinese automakers. Geely, SAIC, and Great Wall purportedly generated between 704 and 683 euros. Looking over Volkswagen's own financial statements explains CAM's rather dramatic estimate.
The group posted 233.4 billion euros in revenue, down 2.2 percent from a year earlier, while vehicle sales fell 10.6 percent, from 6.58 to 5.88 million units. Operating earnings also collapsed, contracting from 5.41 billion euros to merely 71 million. That's a 98.7 percent decline, and this nosedive explains the CAM-estimated operating margin of approximately 0.03 percent.
Photo: Volkswagen Regarding those 8.7 billion euros in special items, including 7.8 in the third quarter alone, the biggest component is a non-cash impairment of Porsche goodwill totaling 6.4 billion euros. Another 1 billion comes from non-cash impairment adjustments on assets held by fully consolidated Chinese companies. Furthermore, additional expenses related to the Osnabruck plant's conversion into a defence manufacturing hub added to the burden.
Goodwill impairments don't represent an equivalent cash payment during the reporting period. Instead, they reduce the accounting value of an asset when a given company reassesses the future economic benefits it expects from it. Even so, a theoretical 3.8 percent operating margin isn't particularly reassuring.
Remember that Volkswagen is one of the biggest automotive groups out there, with Volkswagen also being Europe's largest automaker by sales. The group delivered 8.98 million new vehicles worldwide in 2025, down 0.5 percent from 2024. Per the group's Q3 2026 report, no fewer than 5,781,421 passenger and commercial vehicles were delivered globally in the first nine months of 2026.
Volkswagen isn't the only troubled automaker here. CAM points out that Mercedes-Benz Cars suffered a 56 percent decline in operating EBIT, yet the wider group improved its operating margin from 4.4 to 5.5 percent. BMW, on the other hand, slipped by 2.5 percentage points to 5.6 percent due to weaker contributions from China and substantial investment requirements.
What about Toyota , which is the world's largest automaker by sales? CAM estimates 1,857 euros per vehicle, down 20 percent, whereas Detroit-based General Motors reached 1,670 euros, up 29 percent. Tesla, which is dropping the Cybertruck in 2027, dropped 39 percent to 1,355 euros per vehicle.
Via // auto-institut.de

This DIY Camper Van Is a Homey Mobile Abode Built for Cross-Country Adventures, It's Now for Sale
26 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam
I love a good DIY conversion, not because it's better than a professional one (most aren't), but because they're more attainable to normal people like you and me. Today, I'm checking out a DIY rig that was designed for cross-country adventures.
What we have here is a project based on a 2019 Ram ProMaster 3500 with a 159" wheelbase and a high roof. The two people behind the build are Will and Mary, who are known online as Will and Mary Roam.
As always, let's begin the tour with the exterior. In terms of the wheel and tire combo, the duo kept things simple and opted for standard rims wrapped in road tires.
Most people add ladders to the rear or to the driver's side of the vehicle to be able to climb on the roof. Will and Mary took a different approach and fitted climbing holds on the passenger side, which you can use to climb to the roof, just like you would use in a bouldering gym.
On top of the van, you'll come across three 200 W Renogy solar panels, a Maxxair vent fan, and even a boat hatch skylight. Five wood beams create a small deck that you can chill on – it's the perfect spot to enjoy a coffee while admiring the surrounding views.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam The exciting part of the build is the interior, which feels very homey and snug. Regarding aesthetics, the two opted for cream-colored cabinetry, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, and a black U-Groove ceiling. The look is complemented by butcher block countertops and a faux tile backsplash.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a large curtain to separate the two areas. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases.
You can easily turn the front part of the interior into a seating area. Not only can you turn the two cabin seats around to face the back of the van thanks to the swivel bases, but you can also use two tables when seated.
Straight ahead as you enter, you'll come across a unit with a countertop, a silverware drawer, and a 115-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny removable freezer compartment.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam Beside it, the couple added a decently sized bench that hides a Nature's Head composting toilet on a slide-out, with its backrest integrating two storage compartments. Moreover, above, you'll find two cabinets.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features a propane-powered RecPro oven with a three-burner stove and a deep stainless steel sink with a rotating faucet. What's more, a Maxxair vent fan above draws out the smells and fumes from cooking.
An overhead cabinet, a drawer, a toiletry storage compartment, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. The latter houses a sealed compartment with a propane canister.
The largest storage spot in this van is a floor-to-ceiling unit opposite the kitchen. It offers a closet with hanging space and two large shelves. What's more, the unit's tall door has a full-length mirror on the inside.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam Like in the majority of camper vans, the rear part of the living space is taken up by the bedroom. It boasts a full-size memory foam mattress, two overhead cabinets, charging points, two bunk windows with sliding screens, and a skylight above that's big enough to climb through.
Finally, the space underneath the bed was turned into a garage that's accessible only from the back of the van, after opening the rear doors.
The garage is split into three key parts: two boxes on the sides that accommodate the utility systems, and a big open space in the middle filled with tools and a bunch of other stuff.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 300 Ah Renogy battery bank and a 2,000 W Xantrex inverter. Three charging sources allow you to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC alternator charging while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam On plumbing, the van is equipped with a 39-gallon (147-liter) freshwater tank, a 36-gallon (136-liter) greywater tank, a water pump, an accumulator, a three-stage Clearsource water filtration system, and an outdoor shower connection.
You'll also notice Van Essential storage pockets attached to the inner part of the two doors, which create a lot of useful storage space out of a spot that would've been otherwise useless. Moreover, the passenger-side door holds two towel hooks.
All in all, Will and Mary did a fantastic job with this conversion, packing all the basic comforts most people would need to travel across the United States full-time.
The duo has already put the van to the test by completing a full lap around the country this year, and now they've put it up for sale. According to its Vancamper listing , it has 97,500 miles (156,911 km). Will and Mary are offering it for $59,999 (€54,254), after dropping the price from $65,000.
